messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The horizontal distance a projectile travels after a given time \(t\) is simply the horizontal component of its velocity multiplied by that time:

\[
\text{distance} = v \cos(\theta)\; t
\]

where  
* \(v\) is the launch speed (m s⁻¹),  
* \(\theta\) is the launch angle measured from the horizontal (degrees or radians, but use the same unit for the cosine), and  
* \(t\) is the elapsed time (s).

If you’re interested in the total range (the distance traveled until the projectile lands back on the ground), the classic formula (ignoring air resistance) is

\[
R = \frac{v^{2}\,\sin(2\theta)}{g}
\]

with \(g \approx 9.81\;\text{m s}^{-2}\).

---

### Quick example

Suppose a car (or any projectile) is launched at \(v = 20\;\text{m s}^{-1}\) and \(\theta = 30^\circ\).  
After \(t = 2\;\text{s}\):

\[
\text{distance} = 20 \cos(30^\circ) \times 2 \approx 20 \times 0.866 \times 2 \approx 34.6\;\text{m}
\]

If you want the full range (ignoring air resistance):

\[
R = \frac{20^{2}\,\sin(60^\circ)}{9.81} \approx \frac{400 \times 0.866}{9.81} \approx 35.3\;\text{m}
\]

---

If you have specific numerical values for \(v\), \(\theta\), and \(t\) and would like me to compute the distance for you, just let me know!
